spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: A referee. Not a user of the app, never consented, has no idea their name is being transmitted. Sits outside the candidate contact block, so the header/body split does NOT protect it.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: THE case the NER tier exists for. Given name only, mid-sentence, no adjacent contact cues. A string-match tokenizer keyed on 'Sarah Johnson' misses it. Full text: '...Sarah is an exceptional developer...'

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: Combined with sj-013's name and the title 'Senior Engineering Manager', this identifies a specific named individual at a specific named employer. Quasi-identifier for a third party.

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: Honorific attached. NER may return 'Emily Chen' and drop 'Dr.', producing a partial-span match. Decide whether the harness scores partial spans as TP or FN — recommend FN, since a leaked honorific plus surname is still identifying.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: CRITICAL: this is OUTSIDE basics{}. If the suppressor only covers the contact block, this leaks the candidate's full name via the URL path. Direct test of spec v0.5 open question in method §6.

negative_controls.note: Greek-looking proper noun — plausible PERSON or LOCATION to a weak model.
In projects[0].description. ORG, but a payment vendor, not the candidate's employer.
Volunteer org. Sentence-shaped — 'Code for Good' parses as an imperative clause.
Award title containing a possessive proper noun.

known_traps: Two 'Sarah' in-prose hits (sj-014, sj-017) buried in referee quotes — the field most likely to be treated as harmless body content.
Three third-party individuals' details (sj-013, sj-016, plus titles/employers) that the header/body split does not cover.
Two GitHub URLs outside basics{} (sj-019, sj-020) containing the candidate's name — tests whether URL suppression is field-scoped or global.
basics.summary is deliberately clean of names; confirms the detector is not simply flagging every summary field.
